rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the six-compound elution window while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The retention pattern will identify critical pairs and guide a narrower, faster gradient.
Injection 1 already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient while holding temperature and endpoints fixed to test whether full resolution can be retained in a faster run.

The faster gradient retains maximum CRF but leaves pair 3–4 near the resolution threshold. Raising temperature at the same slope tests whether temperature improves this critical separation while shortening retention.
At 50 C all pairs retain some resolution margin, so test the next shorter gradient. This probes the fastest fully resolved method while preserving injection 3 as a maximum-score fallback.

Reduce the gradient slope to a value between injections 3 and 4, targeting recovery of the critical pair to R ≥ 1.5. The lower endpoint remains well above the estimated last-peak elution composition, so all six compounds should still elute during the gradient.

Raise the starting composition while preserving injection 5’s gradient slope to remove time spent below the elution window. The new start remains below the estimated first-peak elution composition; this tests whether retention can be shortened without losing full resolution.
Slightly flatten injection 6’s gradient to recover the narrowly failing critical pair. Keeping the higher starting composition should preserve much of its retention-time improvement over injection 5.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten retention, keeping the endpoint fixed so the slope becomes slightly shallower. This tests whether the shallower gradient can preserve the critical separation while trimming the early part of the run.

Test a higher starting composition with a substantially shallower gradient to compensate for the critical pair’s sensitivity to the starting fraction. This may shorten the fully resolved run further, although the early pair now needs close monitoring.

Steepen injection 9’s gradient modestly to shorten the last-peak time, using the middle pair’s resolution margin. The early pair should be less affected because it elutes near the start of the gradient.

Use a slope slightly shallower than injection 10 to bring the middle pair back above R = 1.5 while targeting a last-peak time near 3.4 minutes. The trimmed endpoint remains above the estimated final elution composition, allowing a shorter programmed gradient.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a much steeper gradient at lower temperature for a faster separation on the opposite side of a possible middle-pair elution-order reversal. The low starting fraction protects early retention, while the high endpoint ensures strong elution.

Test whether moderate temperature opens the late critical pair in the rapid-gradient regime, while a slightly higher starting fraction shortens retention. The middle pair may have reversed order at this slope, so its separation must be assessed anew.

Test a higher starting fraction at low temperature, which should retain the early compounds more strongly than at 50 C and may change the middle-pair selectivity. This explores a different route to a compact, fully resolved separation while retaining the established maximum-score methods.

Use an intermediate starting fraction and temperature with a shallower gradient to recover the middle-pair separation. This balances early-peak retention against speed and tests a narrower elution window than the previous methods.

Raise temperature one step from injection 10 to test whether its narrowly failing middle pair can reach full resolution with a shorter last-peak time. Monitor the early pair carefully, since its resolution decreased with temperature in earlier runs.

Test whether shifting injection 14’s window upward at the same slope opens the middle pair after an elution-order reversal. Its early pair had substantial resolution margin, although the higher starting fraction risks excessive early compression.

Increase the slope from injection 17 to test whether the apparently reversed middle pair gains the small additional separation needed for full credit. This should also shorten the late-peak retention while leaving the starting composition unchanged.

The steeper gradient slightly reduced the middle-pair resolution, so test a substantially shallower slope at the same starting fraction and temperature. The endpoint should still elute the late compounds promptly, while this run determines whether the high-starting-fraction region can reach full resolution.

Return to the established maximum-score region with a slightly shallower slope than injection 8 to increase the critical pair’s resolution margin. Trimming the endpoint to 0.60 should keep all peaks within the gradient while shortening the programmed gradient to four minutes.

Refine between injections 9 and 10, targeting full resolution with more margin than injection 11 and a last-peak time near 3.5 minutes. This stays in the proven maximum-score region rather than pursuing the less successful high-temperature or high-starting-fraction alternatives.

Test a slightly steeper slope than injection 8 to locate the speed limit at this starting composition. The middle pair is close to its resolution threshold, so retain injection 11 as the fastest demonstrated maximum-score method if this step loses full resolution.

Test a modest temperature increase at injection 6’s slope, with a lower starting fraction than injection 16 to improve early-pair retention. This may recover the middle-pair resolution while shortening the separation; the established maximum-score methods remain the fallback.

With maximum CRF already achieved, refine around injection 20 using a shallower slope to increase the critical-pair resolution margin. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution composition, so the method should retain a compact, fully resolved separation.

Use the final injection to refine within the maximum-score region, with a slope slightly shallower than injection 7 to provide additional middle-pair resolution margin. This should keep all six peaks within the gradient and the last peak below four minutes; injection 11 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.
